answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim a reward. A Sybil attacker must lock real, scarce assets for every fake identity, so creating thousands of accounts ties up capital and risks forfeiture if those accounts coordinate dishonestly. The stake need not prove a person’s uniqueness; it makes influence costly. Like hauling marble across the tundra, an attacker can still wander in, but scaling the attack becomes expensive.
